title: Youghiogheny Resource Managers Building Siding Replacement
description: Youghiogheny Resource Managers Building Siding Replacement. USACE, Pittsburgh District, has an upcoming requirement to replace the siding of the Resource Managers Office at Youghiogheny River Lake. The work described herein shall be performed at the Youghiogheny Resource Managers Office (RMO) building located within the Youghiogheny River Lake project area in Confluence, Pennsylvania. The building currently serves as administrative office space for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. The RMO building was constructed in 1986 and is a multi-level, timber-framed structure built into the hillside overlooking the impoundment side of the dam. The exterior walls consist of 2x6 wood stud framing with 6-inch fiberglass batt insulation (R-19, foil-faced). Interior partitions consist of 2x4 wood studs with 1/2-inch gypsum wallboard. The existing exterior wall assembly consists of 1/2-inch asphalt-saturated fibrous sheathing with 5/8-inch cedar-faced T1-11 plywood siding, for a combined nominal thickness of 1-1/8 inches. Exterior trim and fascia consist of various widths of cedar lumber. The building is supported by cast-in-place concrete footings and 12-inch concrete masonry unit (CMU) foundation walls. The rear wall section and balcony framing are supported by 4 feet-0 inches wide by 5 feet-0 inches deep concrete footings, laminated wood columns (8-3/4 inches x 15 feet-0 inches), and laminated wood beams (8-3/4 inches x 15 feet-0 inches).This project consists of the removal and replacement of the existing exterior wall cladding system. The Contractor shall remove and dispose of the existing T1-11 siding and 1/2-inch asphalt-saturated fibrous sheathing in their entirety. The Contractor shall furnish and install a new exterior wall assembly consisting of 1/2-inch APA-rated structural wood sheathing, a continuous weather-resistive barrier (WRB), 3/8-inch nominal preservative-treated wood furring strips, and 5/16-inch fiber cement lap siding in accordance with manufacturer requirements. The new wall assembly is intended to match the existing wall thickness (approximately 1-1/8 inches) to maintain alignment with existing window and door openings. Minor dimensional variation within normal construction tolerances are acceptable and shall not require modification or resetting of existing windows and doors. The Contractor shall not reset, relocate, or otherwise modify existing windows and doors. Furring strips shall be installed vertically over the WRB at a maximum spacing of 16 inches on center and shall be fastened through the sheathing into wall framing members. Fiber cement siding shall be installed horizontally over the furring strips and fastened through the furring and sheathing into wall framing members. Furring strips are intended to provide a drainage and ventilation cavity and shall not be used as the sole fastening substrate for the fiber cement lap siding. The Contractor shall ensure that all fiber cement lap siding edges are supported by framing members or approved blocking in accordance with manufacturer requirements. The Contractor shall furnish and install all required trim at windows, doors, corners, and transitions. Trim material shall be fiber cement. The cedar hand railing on the balconys is to be new capped PVC or capped composite decking of matching color to fiber cement board siding. The Contractor shall provide complete flashing at all required locations, including but not limited to head flashing at windows and doors, Z-flashing at horizontal joints and transitions, and kick-out flashing at roof-to-wall intersections. All flashing shall be integrated with the WRB in a shingle-lap manner to maintain a continuous drainage plane. The work shall be completed within 180 after written Notice to Proceed. title: USS WICHITA (LCS 13) Docking Selected Restricted Availability (DSRA) - Paint OEM and Technical Services
description: This solicitation is for commercial items and has been prepared in accordance with the format outlined in FAR Subpart 12.6, supplemented with additional information contained in this notice. This announcement constitutes the sole solicitation; quotes are hereby requested. Request for Proposal (RFP) No. N40027-26-R-0008 is issues as a FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION solicitation and is being processed under FAR Part 13 � Simplified Acquisition Procedures and FAR Part 6- Competition Requirements. The applicable North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) code is 325510 � Paint and Coating Manufacturing. Scope of Requirements The Government seeks sources that can provide support as follows: Product Provision: Provide paint, coatings, and preservation products per the Government's Work Statement. Navy Paint Warranty: Paint, coatings, and preservation products must meet the required standards per the attached Navy Paint Warranty (Attachment 3). No Waivers/Subcontracts: The responding vendor must provide the required warranty directly, without waiver or subcontracting. OEM Certification: Offerors must provide proof of Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) certification for the paint and coating systems. Qualified Personnel: Provide Field Service Technical Representatives (FSTR) that meet or exceed the minimum qualifications within the Work Statement in order to perform, inspect, and certify the work stated. Personnel may not be substituted without express written approval by the Government. Hull Coating System: Provide a twelve (12) year antifouling, underwater hull, and boot top coating system that complies with epoxy anticorrosive MIL-PRF-24647, Type I or II, and that complies with antifouling paint MIL-PRF-24647, Type II. Marking Compatibility: Provide preservation products that are suitable for use as hull and boot top markings on the ablative antifoulant paints. Substrate Compatibility: All preservation products must be compatible and have the ability to be applied over any existing coating on like surfaces. Statutory and Licensing Requirements Homeport Statute (10 U.S.C. 7299A): In accordance with the "Homeport Statute", this procurement will solicit offers only from offerors capable of performing the work in the Mayport homeport area. Agreement for Boat Repair (ABR): Offerors must have, or be able to obtain, an Agreement for Boat Repair (ABR) or Government-approved equivalency by the time of contract award. Anticipated Contract Type: Firm-Fixed Price (FFP). Evaluation Method: Price-Only (Among conforming, responsible, and technically acceptable offerors�not a structured Part 15 LPTA). II. Summary of Navy Paint Warranty (Attachment 3) The successful contractor will be required to provide an express Marine Coatings Warranty (incorporated into FAR 52.212-4(o) Addendum) that includes: Two-Year Application Durability: Warranting that the paint is applied correctly so that it lasts a minimum of two (2) years after the date of application, and that the paint is usable up to its expiration date. Premature Failure Remedies: In the event of premature failure (e.g., delaminating, blistering, rust-through, softening, peeling), the Contractor shall furnish, at no cost to the Government, all materials and technical representative services necessary to recoat the failed area at any domestic or foreign location designated by the Government. Hull Scamping: Providing scamping of the underwater hull at no cost to the Government if more than twenty (20) percent of the underwater hull is heavily fouled due to poor performance of the antifouling within two (2) years of application. Misapplication Notice: The warranty is not voided by shipyard misapplication unless the Contractor's technical representative provides timely notice (written within 24 hours of verbal notice, and no later than 8 hours after the event) specifying the affected areas and required remedial actions. III. Questions for Industry The notice of interest should include a brief description of your company, its capabilities as they relate to the requirements, and answers to the following specific questions. Please limit your response to no more than five (5) pages (excluding certifications or licenses). Is your company a small or large business as defined by the Small Business Administration (SBA) under NAICS code 325510 (Paint and Coating Manufacturing)? If a small business, please specify your socioeconomic status (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), Women-Owned (WOSB), HUBZone, Veteran-Owned (VOSB), or Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned (SDVOSB)). How many employees does your company have? Does your company have an active website? If so, what is your company's website address? Does your company have a satisfactory performance record for this type of marine preservation work? Please provide examples of relevant and recent (within the last three years) past performance. Is your company able to provide both the desired paint product AND the manufacturer's guarantee/warranty without waiver or subcontracting, as detailed in the "Scope of Requirements" and "Navy Paint Warranty"? Given the complexity of the work described in this announcement, please describe your company's historical experience completing services on similar ship classes (e.g., Littoral Combat Ships or similar naval vessels) or briefly describe how your company is capable of meeting these requirements by the time of contract award. Given the complexity and size of the work described, does your company plan to submit a proposal/quote in response to the anticipated solicitation for the paint coatings and technical services of USS THE WICHITA (LCS 13)? IV. Submission Instructions Information provided shall be treated as Business Sensitive or Confidential to the responder, exempt from public release under the Freedom of Information Act. All information shall be provided free of charge to the Government. SERMC may request further information regarding the capabilities of respondents to meet the requirements set forth in the announcement. Where and When to Submit All proposals must be submitted electronically via email with the subject line: "USS WICHITA (LCS 13) Docked Selected Restricted Availability (DSRA) - Paint OEM N4002726R0008". Submission Deadline: September 21, 2026, at 11:00 AM (1100 hours) SERMC Local Time. Submit to the following Points of Contact (POCs): sermc_c423.4_lcs_gold@us.navy.mil andres.m.walsh.civ@us.navy.mil anthony.r.turner14.civ@us.navy.mil jonathan.lebron.civ@us.navy.mil ***FULL DELIVERY OF MATERIALS ARE DUE TO THE DELIVERY ADDRESS IN JACKSONVILLE, FL LOCATED AT THE CONTRACTOR�S FACILITY WHERE THE SHIP WILL BE DRYDOCKED, 28 October 2026 ***PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: BAE SYSTEMS JACKSONVILLE SHIP REPAIR LLC, 8500 HECKSCHER DR, JACKSONVILLE FL 32226 Contracting Office Address: USS WICHITA (LCS 13) SERM-803-27 OEM Paint Southeast Regional Maintenance Center Building 1488, Naval Station Mayport Jacksonville, Florida 32228

title: Army CONUS Enterprise (ACE) Land Mobile Radio (LMR) � Motorola OEM Extended Warranty and Maintenance Support for Fort Novosel, AL and Holston Army Ammunition Plant (HAAP), TN
description: NOTICE OF INTENT-SOURCES SOUGHT The Defense Information Systems Agency /Defense Information Technology Contracting Organization intends to negotiate a sole source contract with Motorola Solutions, Inc. A sole source Justification & Approval document is being coordinated and, upon approval, a copy of it will be posted to SAM.gov to comply with the public display requirements of FAR 6.301. The proposed contract action is for Army CONUS Enterprise (ACE) Land Mobile Radio (LMR) - Motorola Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) Extended Warranty and Maintenance Support for Fort Novosel, Alabama, and Holston Army Ammunition Plant (HAAP), Tennessee. The period of performance is September 30, 2026, September 29, 2027, with one, one year option period. The requirement provides continued OEM extended warranty and associated maintenance support for Government-accepted Motorola LMR equipment and components covered by the applicable OEM warranty entitlement. Support includes OEM warranty administration; OEM technical support; diagnosis of covered equipment failures; repair or replacement of covered components; Return Material Authorization processing; warranty-related software and firmware updates made available under OEM entitlement; replacement components required to fulfill warranty obligations; applicable licensing; transportation and shipping associated with warranty actions; and coordination and tracking of warranty actions through closure. The contractor is required to provide OEM-backed technical and lifecycle support to ensure the continued operation of the existing Motorola LMR systems and maintain warranty coverage throughout the period of performance. At this time, the incumbent contractor Motorola Solutions, Inc.(Motorola) is the only source capable of fulfilling the requirement for OEM extended warranty and maintenance support for the existing Motorola LMR systems and associated equipment. As the OEM, Motorola, possesses the proprietary technical data, system-specific knowledge, OEM repair capabilities, software and firmware support, replacement components, licensing, and warranty authority necessary to provide continued OEM-backed coverage for the installed Motorola equipment. Awarding this requirement to another source would not provide the required Motorola OEM extended warranty coverage and could jeopardize the Government�s ability to maintain OEM-supported maintenance, compatibility, and lifecycle support for the existing Motorola LMR infrastructure and equipment. Such an outcome would introduce significant risks to mission-critical communications, operational readiness, and the security of Army Enterprise LMR systems. The statutory authority for other than full and open competition is 10 USC 2304 (c) (1), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1, only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Companies who believe they can provide this service must indicate their interest in writing within 15 days of this notification and include a detailed capability statement. No reimbursement for any cost connected with providing capability information will be provided. All responsible sources will be considered in evaluating the determination to issue a sole-source contract. Quotations or proposals received in response to this notice cannot be accepted since this synopsis cannot be considered a request for quote or a request for proposal. A solicitation will NOT be posted to SAM.gov due to the sole source nature of the requirement. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 334210, Telephone Apparatus Manufacturing, will be used for determining company size status. CONTRACT/PROGRAM BACKGROUND: The Motorola OEM Extended Warranty and Maintenance Support requirement is currently being performed under the following contract: Contract Number: HC108424P0005 Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Incumbent and Size: Motorola Solutions, Inc. � Large Business CAGE: 78205 Method of Previous Acquisition: Sole Source Period of Performance: July 31, 2024 through September 30, 2026 SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS: The Contractor shall be the OEM, Motorola Solutions, Inc., or possess the necessary OEM authorization and capabilities to provide the required Motorola OEM extended warranty and maintenance support for the covered LMR systems and associated equipment in accordance with the PWS. title: Guatemala – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Asistencia Técnica para la implementación de la Agenda de inversiones Global Gateway en Guatemala – Global Gateway Facility Guatemala
description: En 2021, la Comisión Europea lanzó la estrategia de inversiones Global Gateway, que tiene como objetivo fomentar inversiones de gran calibre en infraestructura verde y digital en los países socios, con soluciones innovadoras y de calidad, creando al mismo tiempo valor añadido local y promoviendo el crecimiento económico, el empleo y la cohesión social. Durante la III Cumbre UE-CELAC, celebrada en julio de 2023, los dirigentes de ambas regiones reafirmaron su compromiso de reforzar la asociación birregional, reconociendo la importancia de la Agenda de Inversiones Global Gateway. Dicho compromiso fue renovado durante la IV Cumbre UE-CELAC celebrada en noviembre de 2025. El objetivo general de esta acción es contribuir a la implementación de inversiones sostenibles y transformadoras en los sectores de transición verde y digital en Guatemala, donde haya un interés común europeo y de la agenda de desarrollo de Guatemala, y ello en el marco de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway, asegurando su alineación con las prioridades estratégicas del país y fomentando un desarrollo inclusivo y sostenible. La Asistencia Técnica contribuirá a: mejorar la alineación, coordinación y monitoreo de las iniciativas implementadas en el marco de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway en Guatemala; promover un marco regulatorio e institucional que favorezca la inversión sostenible en los sectores prioritarios de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway; impulsar proyectos de inversión sostenibles, transformadores y sensibles a la igualdad de género y a las buenas prácticas internacionales en materia de derechos y protección del medioambiente en los sectores prioritarios y a posicionar los intereses del sector privado europeo en el marco de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway para Guatemala. Sin excluir otras potenciales áreas de trabajo prioritarias para la UE y Guatemala, y reconociendo la flexibilidad dinámica de la estrategia Global Gateway, las áreas prioritarias para Guatemala actualmente incluyen transición verde (transporte sostenible, energía renovable e integración eléctrica regional, economía circular, gestión sostenible de recursos naturales y residuos) y transición digital (conectividad, gobernanza digital, ciberseguridad, innovación digital, observación de la Tierra, inteligencia artificial).

title: Ireland – Construction work – RFT 02/26/GM - Works Contractor and PSCS for ATU Dublin Road EEDPP2 Energy Retrofit at Atlantic Technological University at the Galway City Campus
description: Atlantic Technological University (ATU) is seeking suitably qualified and experienced contractors to undertake an energy retrofit project at its Galway City Dublin Road Campus. The project comprises the retrofit of approximately 4,425m² of the original 1972 building and forms part of the Higher Education Authority (HEA) and Sustainable Energy Authority of Ireland (SEAI) funded Energy Efficiency and Decarbonisation Pathfinder Project (EEDPP2). The works include building fabric upgrades, roof and window replacement, ventilation improvements, lighting and controls upgrades, and the installation of a medium-temperature air-source heat pump, with existing gas boilers retained for peak demand and backup. The project aims to improve energy efficiency, reduce carbon emissions, extend the building's operational life, enhance occupant comfort, increase the use of renewable technologies, and achieve a minimum B1 BER rating. The existing building is a reinforced concrete framed structure currently served by the campus central heating system and a combination of natural and mechanical ventilation systems.

title: Ireland – Electrical engineering installation works – TII522 Electrical Renewals Luas Works (Low Voltage) IMPQQ
description: TII intends to enter into Multi Party Framework Agreement for Luas Electrical Renewals and Upgrade Works (Low Voltage) for the Luas Light Rail System. This IMPQQ competition aims to identify and shortlist highly qualified electrical contractors with proven electrical expertise and experience in Low Voltage (LV) electrical systems for light rail or heavy rail infrastructure, specifically in the design, installation, testing, commissioning, and compliance of railway electrical systems at LV level. This framework, when established, will be available to TII to draw down from it on a Call-Off Contract basis, (i.e. PW-CF2 or PW-CF4). The Applicant must demonstrate a strong track record of delivering complex electrical works in live operational rail environments, ensuring safety, quality, reliability, and full regulatory compliance. The Applicant must demonstrate their experience in the design, installation, testing, commissioning of safety critical electrical systems in live railway environments and compliance of various railway electrical LV systems. The IMPQQ details where TII allows subcontracting. Applicants must demonstrate their experience working in live railway environment and must be capable of acting as or procuring suitably competent persons to act as the Project Supervisor for the Design Process (PSDP) and the Project Supervisor for the Construction Stage (PSCS) in accordance with Irish health and safety legislation. TII are inviting expressions of interest from interested parties to be selected to tender with a view to entering into the Contract. Applicants are referred to the Information Memorandum and Prequalification Questionnaire (IMPQQ) which provides additional information in relation to the competition. Provided that there is a sufficient number of suitable Applicants, TII intends to invite the number of Applicants (as indicated in this IMPQQ) to tender. title: Technical Assistance to Embed Renewable Integration in Madagascar Mining Permits
description: La description de l'appel d'offres ainsi que les documents de soumission sont également disponibles en français. Veuillez consulter les pièces jointes pour plus d'informations. Following the reopening of mining permits in 2026, Madagascar has an opportunity to shape how new mining investments source power. While mining and environmental regulations are in place, renewable energy integration is not yet embedded within licensing and permitting requirements. The assignment will support the Government of Madagascar to design, adopt and implement a Green Mining Energy Framework that embeds renewable energy requirements into mining licensing, environmental permitting and ESIA processes. Key outputs include a diagnostic and design options package, a Green Mining Energy Framework and supporting guidance for government adoption, and an implementation and compliance package with templates, monitoring tools and capacity-building support. The project aims to reduce future diesel dependence in the mining sector and support lower-emission mining development in Madagascar. Interested suppliers are invited to review the documentation provided in this notice, and submit their applications to: targetedfund@ukpact.co.uk

title: Unlocking Commercial and Industrial Captive Renewable Energy in Uganda: Market Sizing and Regulatory Reform
description: The UK Government's Partnering for Accelerated Climate Transitions (UK PACT) programme is inviting proposals from qualified suppliers or consortia to deliver technical assistance to Uganda's Electricity Regulatory Authority (ERA). Uganda's electricity sector is predominantly powered by renewable energy and demand is growing rapidly. However, uptake of commercial and industrial (C&I) captive renewable energy remains limited due to regulatory gaps, insufficient market data, and barriers to investment. This is particularly significant given the growing role of behind-the-meter renewable energy as a means of reducing diesel reliance, improving energy security, and supporting economic growth. The assignment will support ERA, in partnership with the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development (MEMD) and electricity distributors UEDCL, WENRECO and KIS, to strengthen the enabling environment for C&I captive renewable energy. The work will establish an evidence base on market demand, existing captive generation and grid capacity, review Uganda's regulatory framework and international best practice, and develop targeted regulatory and market-enabling solutions. Key outputs are expected to include recommendations for a mid-tier regulatory framework, updated settlement and implementation guidance, standardised commercial documentation, and financing pathways to improve project bankability. The project aims to increase private-sector investment in captive renewable energy, accelerate deployment, reduce dependence on diesel generation, and strengthen Uganda's energy security and grid resilience. Interested suppliers are invited to review the documentation provided in this notice, and submit their applications to: targetedfund@ukpact.co.uk

B. HARDWARE APPLIANCES AND HARDWARE MAINTENANCE Data Diode Appliances: Fiber-optic hardware-enforced one-way data transfer appliances (FDD10G Series) including annual hardware warranty and associated software maintenance. Cross-Domain Access (CDA) & Verifier Hardware: G2CI Cross Domain Access V2 custom hardware and hardware maintenance (1079H-CDA Series) and High-Speed Verifier turnkey appliances (HSVT Series). title: Z1DA--NRM-CONST 526-21-105 - REPLACE FIRE ALARM SYSTEM (FY27 NRM)
description: THIS ANNOUNCEMENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. THE GOVERNMENT WILL NOT PAY NOR REIMBURSE ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH RESPONDING TO THIS REQUEST. THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. This is a "REQUEST FOR INFORMATION" only. This Sources Sought Notice is for informational and planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation or commitment by the Government. This notice is intended strictly for market research. This is not a Request for Proposal or an announcement of a solicitation, and no solicitation package exists at this time. Your responses will be used solely for market research purposes of the Government. The Government will not pay for any materials provided in response to this notice and submittals will not be returned to the sender. Requests for a solicitation will not receive a response. Responses to this Sources Sought must be in writing. The James J. Peters VA Medical Center, 130 West Kingsbridge Rd, Bronx, NY 10468, has a requirement for construction services. Project Number 526-21-105 Replace Fire Alarm System. The layout is a campus with 14 buildings located on approximately 30 acres and over 1 million square feet of floor space. The existing fire alarm system is original to the new building construction circa 1980. The intent of this project is to install a new parallel fire alarm system in accordance with current NFPA and VA requirements and then once the new system is accepted remove the existing system and repair all walls, ceilings and equipment, etc. as necessary. Provide all labor, material, equipment, and supervision to perform the following: Install a new fire alarm system parallel to the existing system. This includes all new conduits and boxes, fiber optics, wiring, devices, control panels, annunciators, etc. Temporarily mount the new panels and annunciators above the existing so the new system can be tested for full and proper operation while the existing system remains operational. The following locations and equipment will primarily remain and be used as part of the new system: Building 100 Sterile Processing in Wing GA, Emergency Department in Wing 1C, Mental Health in Wing 6C. Fisher Houses 1 and 2. New control panels and communications to the control panel in Building 107 are required, existing equipment to remain but some new devices are added to bring up to code. After initial testing and acceptance of the new system, move the new panels and annunciators into the existing cabinets or boxes and relocate wiring. Remove all the old conduits and boxes, fiber optics and wiring, devices, control panels and annunciators, etc. Repair all walls, ceilings and other architectural features damaged from the installation of the new system and removal of the old. Refer to the design drawings, specification and acquisition package details. Refer to 01 00 00 General Requirements for a more detailed statement of bid. The magnitude of this project is between $10,000,000.00 and $20,000,000.00. The NAICS Code is 238210 "Electrical Contractors and Other Wiring Installation Contractors", with a size standard of $19M. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement to include bonding capacity which shall be considered by the James J. Peters VA Medical Center. Please include the socio-economic status of your business. This is not a solicitation. If there is sufficient interest, a solicitation shall be posted on SAM.gov. Please send all inquiries to: Akkil.Kurian@va.gov by 12:00 EST Monday, September 21, 2026. Phone calls will not be accepted.

title: Intent to Sole Source - a Preventative Maintenance Agreement (PMA) for the Alpha Omega Machine
description: This is a Notice of Intent, not a request for proposal. The National Institute of Health, Clinical Center (NIH-CC) intends to negotiate on an other than full and open competition basis with the following vendor: Alpha Omega. Acquisition Description: The Department of Perioperative Medicine and Dr. Zaghloul is requesting a Preventative Maintenance Agreement (PMA) for the Alpha Omega Machine which is a micro-electrode recording and stimulation system for deep brain stimulation surgery. The purpose of this purchase is to provide the Surgical Neurology Branch with equipment support for a multi-modality micro-electrode recording system that can capture single-unit spiking data, local field potential data, simultaneous surface EEG data, and that can provide real-time online analyses and triggered and patterned electrical stimulation. The PMA for this piece of equipment supports protocol 11-N-0211. The statutory authority for this sole source requirement is 41 U.S.C. 253(c) (1) as implemented by FAR 6.302-1 only one responsible source and no other supply of service will satisfy agency requirements. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. description:

The Trust intends to establish a two-year call-off contract, with the option to extend for up to a further two years in two separate one-year increments (1+1), to support backlog reduction and improve timely patient access to services. The contract start date is estimated to be 1st April 2027.

Suppliers must be able to deliver echocardiography services in line with the Trust’s specification and clinical requirements, ensuring compliance with relevant quality, governance, and service standards.

title: Lackland Laundry and Linen
description: UPDATED TO INCLUDE Q&A's. New Closing date of 21 Sep 2026. Combined Synopsis/Solicitation for Lackland Laundry & Linen Services Solicitation Number: HT9408-26-Q-E029 Agency: Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA), Healthcare Contracting Division - South (HCD-S) Classification Code: S209 - Housekeeping - Laundry/Drycleaning NAICS Code: 812320 - Drycleaning and Laundry Services (except Coin-Operated) Set-Aside: 100% Small Business (SBA Size Standard: $8.0 Million) Response Due Date: September 21, 2026, 12:00 PM Central Standard Time Place of Performance: Services will be performed for the Wilford Hall Ambulatory Surgical Center (WHASC) and other outlying clinics at Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA) Lackland and JBSA Randolph, Texas. Description of Services: The Defense Health Agency is seeking a contractor to provide all necessary personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, and transportation for non-personal, medical-grade bulk laundry and dry-cleaning services. This is a competitive follow-on to Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) HT940823A0002. The required services include, but are not limited to: Bulk medical laundry processing, sorting, and delivery. Microfiber laundry services. Special item laundry services for non-standard clinical linens and lab coats. Specialized stain wash services for heavily soiled linens. Veterinary laundry services, kept separate from human clinical linens. Bulk laundry services for the JBSA Randolph Clinic. The contractor must adhere to strict quality control, infection control, and transportation standards, including guidelines from the CDC, OSHA, and the Healthcare Laundry Accreditation Council (HLAC). This includes maintaining specific air pressure boundaries in processing facilities and following sanitation protocols for transport vehicles. The Government will award a single, Firm-Fixed-Price contract. The award will be made to the responsible offeror whose proposal is compliant, receives a "Pass" for Technical Capability, and represents the Best Value to the Government based on a comparative tradeoff between Past Performance and Price. Future Scope Adaptability: Please note there is a future possibility of adding laundry and linen services, increasing linen volumes, or including additional outlying clinics/facilities within the 59th Medical Wing's area of responsibility via bilateral modification. Submission Instructions: Proposals must be submitted electronically via email to the points of contact listed in the solicitation. Please refer to the attached "Instructions to Offerors" document for detailed proposal structure, page limits, and submission requirements. All questions regarding this solicitation must be submitted via email no later than September 3, 2026.

title: Remedial Investigation and Action at 16 AOCs at Annette Island, AK
description: The FAA has a requirement for engineering services necessary to perform remedial investigation (RI), and remedial action (RA) activities at multiple Environmental Cleanup (ECU) Program sites and areas of concern (AOCs), at 16 different AOCs, at the former Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Station on Annette Island Reserve, Alaska. Special Considerations: - This project will be performed on the Annette Island Reserve which is under the authority of the Metlakatla Indian Community (MIC). Interested vendors must have had experience in the last 10 years with the regulations of the Metlakatla Indian Community Environmental Council as well as, experience working within the Metlakatla Indian Community policies for worker and business permits, as well as materials purchase. - MIC requires all visitors to apply for a visitor permit. Visitors who will be in the community for longer than two weeks will need to apply for a residency permit. - All excavation backfill material must be purchased from MIC. No organic materials, including seed mixes, can be brought to the island. - Global positioning system (GPS) service and telecommunications are unavailable in many areas on the Metlakatla Peninsula. Satellite communications, mobile GPS antenna stations, walkie-talkies, and/or other technology resources may be needed to verify target locations, allow for communications across Contractor teams and with FAA representatives, and ensure safety of the field team. - Most sites are historical in nature and no longer serve to support FAA�s National Airspace System (NAS). Most sites were abandoned and/or demolished by the FAA in the 1960s, 1970s, and 1980s. While significant clearing occurred at many of the target sites in 2023 and 2024, the Contractor should anticipate that considerable overgrowth (mostly alder and brush) or new growth is present at these sites. - The Contractor must abide by all applicable laws, codes, regulations, and guidance, and is required to perform all work in full compliance with federal, state (as applicable outside Annette Island), and local laws, codes, and regulations. The Contractor must ensure that all activities executed by their personnel, subcontractors, and suppliers are in full compliance with said laws, codes, regulations, and guidance. Any incident of noncompliance must immediately be brought to the attention of the FAA CO. Nothing in this SOW relieves the Contractor of their responsibility to comply with all applicable laws and regulations. - Prior projects encountered multiple issues due to the logistics of getting sample shipments off Annette Island and onto Gravina Island to be transported to the laboratory. The weather, airplane schedules, ferry schedules, staffing reductions and freight office closures at Alaska Airlines, can all impact the transportation of sample shipments. The 200mg/kg concentration for the MIC cleanup level for DRO and RRO makes the use of a PID/FID to screen excavations for boundary obtainment difficult. The matrix interference from organic materials, obtaining reliable usable analytical results to determine if an excavation has reached its boundary has been difficult to obtain in a reasonable timeframe. At times the laboratory data has not been usable due to matrix interference, holding time exceedance, or turnaround time delays. Summary Statement of Work: - The Contractor must submit a Work Plan that describes the Contractor's detailed approach for the performance of this contract. The work plan must be based upon this SOW. The Contractor shall review the two most recent reports for work performed for the FAA and assume that the same quality will go into the work plan. - The FAA expects that the Contractor will encounter heavy vegetation in the study areas. Old growth vegetation (assumed for purposes of this SOW as trees having a diameter of 18 inches or more at chest height) may also be encountered. If such trees are found to be present at any of the work sites, the Contractor shall coordinate with FAA and MIC to have important old growth specimens tagged. All tagged trees will be protected to the maximum extent practicable. Nevertheless, FAA expects that the Contractor will make all efforts necessary to complete the scoped activities and objectives while protecting old growth vegetation. - Clearing of vegetation is expected to the extent necessary to fully evaluate the areas of interest pursuant to this SOW. The Contractor shall use a mulching mower, brush mulcher, or similar equipment to avoid the need to haul/dispose downed vegetation. - A navigation aid outage will not be required to perform the SOW at these sites. - For all excavation confirmation laboratory samples, the Contractor shall perform Silica Gel Cleanup (SGCU) of samples by the laboratory as part of the analytical process in accordance with ADEC�s Technical Memorandum-21-001 Biogenic Interference and SGCU (December 22, 2021) to distinguish petrogenic contaminant sources from biogenic conditions. - The Contractor shall select a laboratory and processes capable of achieving sufficiently low MDLs to allow for direct comparison of analytical results to relevant CULs. - There is a discontinuous peat layer at most sites. The peat is saturated with petroleum. The peat layer when encountered and determined to be contaminated will be excavated and disposed of off island. The peat needs to be removed to help achieve reductions in the groundwater concentrations over time. - Prior investigations found that the petroleum contamination was primarily found in the top 1 to 2 feet of the AOCs, trapped in the muskeg and the top several inches of the clay layer under the muskeg. The FAA assumes that the sites will be excavated from the current edge of the pad outward and downward until extents of the petroleum contamination are found. - Prior projects encountered multiple issues due to the logistics of getting sample shipments off Annette Island and onto Gravina Island to be transported to the laboratory. The weather, airplane schedules, ferry schedules, staffing reductions and freight office closures at Alaska Airlines, can all impact the transportation of sample shipments. In order to better understand the market for this potential requirement, the FAA requests the following information from interested Small Businesses: 1. Name of Company (the resultant Prime contractor that may ultimately be awarded the subsequent contract) 2. Address 3. Point of Contact name, email address and telephone number 4. UEI Number 5. Relevant experience on similar projects within the last five years. Please provide specific contract numbers, contact names and email information to support claimed capabilities. Please submit your capability statement and the above information to Sonia.o.holguin@faa.gov no later than September 21, 2026 at 1200 Central Daylight Savings Time. Failure to respond to this pre-solicitation will preclude a Contractor�s ability to receive a copy of the future solicitation. Limit complete responses to no more than five pages. Information will not be released; however, mark PROPRIETARY on all documents submitted, as applicable.

title: Large Capacity Nonhuman Primate Cage and Rack Washer
description: This is a Notice of Intent notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The Division of Veterinary Resources (DVR) within the National Institute of Health (NIH), Office of Research Services (ORS) requires the procurement, delivery, installation, commissioning, and training associated with the replacement of the existing Tecniplast large-capacity nonhuman primate cage and rack washer supporting nonhuman primate housing operations at the NIH main campus, Bethesda, Maryland with minimal disruption to ongoing animal care activities. DVR requires replacement of an end-of-life cage and rack washer that supports nonhuman primate (NHP) housing operations. The existing unit, manufactured by the same company that manufactures the proposed replacement system, has been in continuous service for approximately twenty (20) years and has exceeded its expected service life. The unit is experiencing increasingly frequent failures, resulting in elevated maintenance costs, operational disruptions, and material risk to research continuity. The replacement system shall provide high-capacity, pass-through washing and sanitization for NHP cages, transport equipment, racks, feeders, enrichment devices, and ancillary husbandry equipment and shall support daily cage-wash operations. All products provided under this award must support compliance with the Animal Welfare Act (AWA), Public Health Service Policy on Humane Care and Use of Laboratory Animals, the Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals, AAALAC International Accreditation standards and Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) requirements. This is a Notice of Intent; the National Institutes of Health (NIH) intends to negotiate a sole source contract for the Tecniplast USA model Atlantis EVO XL with: TECNIPLAST USA, INC. 1345 Enterprise Dr. West Chester, PA 19380-5964 Unique Entity Identifier (UEI): QHF3J4MS24H4 The statutory authority for this sole source requirement is 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1) as implemented by FAR 6.302.1(b)(1)(i) �Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services will satisfy agency Requirements.�, no substitutions possible. Since the intent is to procure this on a sole source basis, no solicitation will be posted to Contract Opportunities, https://www.sam.gov. REQUIREMENT: The contractor shall furnish all labor, materials, equipment, and transportation necessary to deliver, assemble, install, commission, and validate a complete and operational large-capacity cage and rack washer system at the designated DVR NHP facility location at the NIH main campus in Bethesda, Maryland. Minimum performance requirements include: Equipment: Commercial-grade, pass-through cage and rack washer with clean and dirty side barrier operation; stainless steel construction; dual interlocked tempered-glass pass-through doors with inflatable gasket system; capacity for large NHP cages, racks, transport carts, feeders, and ancillary equipment; steam-heated operation; dedicated wash and rinse circuits; separate alkaline and acid wash tanks; automated detergent dosing; tool-free self-cleaning filtration; multiple oscillating wash arm assemblies; chamber lighting; and emergency stop devices accessible from both sides. The system must exhaust through the facility's existing HVAC system and achieve a processing cycle time of approximately 20 minutes for large NHP rack loads. Controls and Monitoring: Touchscreen operator interface with multi-level password-protected controls; remote diagnostics capability; utility monitoring and consumption tracking; data logging and export functionality; Ethernet connectivity; self-start or scheduled operation functionality; and alarm monitoring and troubleshooting. Utilities: 480V/60Hz/3-phase electrical service; steam heating; domestic water supply; facility drainage connection; exhaust integration with the facility's existing HVAC system (no independent exhaust pathway or roof penetration); temperature-controlled wastewater discharge; and pH-controlled wastewater discharge. Installation and Commissioning: Coordination with DVR and ORF personnel; pre-installation site survey; equipment delivery, assembly, installation, and utility connection; startup and commissioning; operational testing documentation; Site Acceptance Testing (SAT) verifying installation, operational performance, utility and control functionality, alarm operation, wash cycle performance, and documentation delivery. Equipment shall not be considered accepted until all SAT deficiencies are corrected. Training: Onsite training for DVR personnel covering equipment operation, routine and preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, safety features, emergency procedures, and control system reporting. Training materials to be provided electronically. Warranty: Minimum two-year manufacturer warranty covering parts, labor, travel, and technical support from date of successful commissioning and acceptance, including remote technical support and onsite service when required. Required Deliverables: Equipment submittal package; shop drawings and utility requirements; Operations and Maintenance Manuals; Preventive Maintenance Schedule; Startup and Commissioning Report; Site Acceptance Test Report; Training Documentation; and Warranty Documentation. DVR�s SPECIFIC REQUIRMENTS: DVR has two mission-essential facility-driven requirements: HVAC-Integrated Exhaust Compatibility: The current NIH DVR nonhuman primate cage washroom was designed and constructed with the cage and rack washer exhausting through the building's existing HVAC system. This infrastructure configuration does not include a dedicated roof exhaust penetration or independent exhaust duct pathway for the cage wash equipment. Processing Cycle Time: The existing cage and rack washer operates at a processing cycle time of approximately 45 minutes per load. DVR has determined this to be operationally inefficient and inadequate to support current NHP husbandry throughput requirements without scheduling constraints and delays that adversely affect daily animal care operations. DVR has established a maximum processing cycle time of approximately 20 minutes as a minimum performance requirement for the replacement system. This cycle time is necessary to process the required daily volume of NHP cage wash loads within the operational constraints of the cage washroom and DVR staffing schedules, and to restore the operational efficiency degraded by the current aging unit. Market Research (Market Research Report and Acquisition Plan, separately documented) for the replacement of the large capacity and wash rack for NHP, full and open competition, vendor neutral, performance based salient features, yielded multiple commercial manufacturers (Tecniplast USA, Getinge USA, STERIS Corporation (Amsco), Allentown Inc., Alternative Design Manufacturing and Supply and others) with established product lines of large-capacity, pass-through cage and rack washer systems designed for laboratory animal facility environments. All identified vendors offer systems that generally meet the baseline performance characteristics common to this equipment category, including pass-through barrier design, stainless steel construction, steam heating, dual wash tanks, automated detergent dosing and touchscreen controls, remote diagnostics and 480V/3-phase electrical compatibility. However, the systems (Tecniplast USA, excepted) require a dedicated, independent exhaust pathway terminating at the building exterior, typically via a roof penetration. Installing a dedicated roof exhaust for an alternative unit in the existing NIH facility would require significant structural modifications, including penetration of the roof assembly, addition of dedicated ductwork through finished building spaces, and associated mechanical and structural engineering work. These modifications would result in substantial additional cost to the Government, extended construction time

title: Locate & Repair a Water Main Leak at USCG Cutter Chena Moorings in Hickman, KY
description: The United States Coast Guard is accepting proposals for qualified individuals or firms to locate and repair a water main leak at USCG Cutter Chena moorings in Hickman, KY. Arrangements for visiting the site may be made by contacting: MKC Brandon Upchurch Email: brandon.m.upchurch@uscg.mil Telephone: (907) 942-7653 The work is located at: U.S. Coast Guard Cutter Chena, 503 Hall St. Hickman, KY 42050. This will be a firm-fixed priced purchase order awarded to the lowest priced technically acceptable offer. The evaluation factors are: - Price - Technical Acceptability - Past Performance Make sure to provide your price, technical approach, and past performance with your quote. The Government will evaluate the past performance of each offeror to determine the degree of confidence that the offeror will successfully perform the contract requirements. Evaluation will consider the relevance, quality, and timeliness of prior work as demonstrated through submitted references and independent government sources. Offerors, if they wish, can also provide information on problems encountered on the identified contracts and the offeror�s corrective actions. The source selection authority shall determine the relevance of similar past performance information. Submit quotes to Joel.S.Ivy@uscg.mil by the date and time listed in this solicitation. title: Basic Ordering Agreement for Steel
description: SOLICITATION EXECUTIVE SUMMARY 1. THREE-STEP PROCUREMENT FRAMEWORK The Government will procure raw metal stock and components requirements utilizing a three-step process: Step One (Combined Synopsis/Solicitation): A separate Pre-solicitation Notice will not be issued; this synopsis is combined with the solicitation on SAM.gov in accordance with FAR Subpart 12.6. Individual order-level Request for Quotes (RFQs) under this Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) will be competed exclusively within the qualified pool and will not be synopsized, ensuring rapid execution. Clauses are in effect through FAC 2026-01. The primary NAICS code is 331110 (Iron and Steel Mills and Ferroalloy Manufacturing; Size Standard: 1,500 employees). Other codes are listed in Attachment 001 - Purchase Description, and the Product Service Code is 9515 (Plate, sheet, strip, foil, and leaf). Step Two (Master BOA Execution): The BOA Request for Proposal (RFP) will be released once for qualifications. The Government will execute no-cost, multi-award BOAs to responsible offerors whose proposals are compliant with Section L and rated "Acceptable" under Section M. BOAs are valid for up to five (5) years. NOTE: This RFP is the only opportunity to obtain a raw metal stock and components BOA. Proposals will not be accepted or executed at any other time. If a contractor wishes to participate in any future raw metal stock and component orders, they must respond to this initial RFP. Step Three (Order-Level Competition): As recurring supply needs arise, the PCO will issue competitive, order-level RFQs to the BOA pool. To participate, contractors must hold an active master BOA as of the RFQ closing date. Orders will result in individual, competitive Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contracts (Orders) under FAR 16.703. 2. SCOPE Contractors will provide commercial products supporting the following CONUS sites including but not limited to: Blue Grass Army Depot (BGAD) Pine Bluff Arsenal (PBA) Letterkenny Munitions Center (LEMC) Crane Army Ammunition Activity (CAAA) Tooele Army Depot (TEAD) McAlester Army Ammunition Plant (MCAAP) Joint Manufacturing and Technology Center (JMTC) Tank-Automotive and Armaments Command (TACOM) 3. SUBCONTRACTING FLEXIBILITY Offerors must demonstrate technical capability within the scope of Attachment 001: Product Description. Capability may be achieved with or without subcontractors. In Step Three order-level proposals, contractors are not bound to the subcontractors proposed in Step Two but must propose resources necessary to perform each individual order. 4. BASIS FOR AGREEMENT EXECUTION The Government will execute no-cost, multi-award BOAs to responsible offerors with compliant proposals (Section L) rated "Acceptable" (Section M). NOTE: The Government reserves the right to waive the Compliance Review if in its best interest. The Government intends to execute BOAs on initial proposals without discussion. It reserves the right to negotiate if in its best interest but will only do so with offerors whose proposals do not contain significant informational deficiencies. LEGAL NOTICE: This master BOA process is not a competitive acquisition; the source selection procedures of FAR Part 15 do not apply. No pricing is requested or evaluated at this stage. Execution of a BOA does not constitute a contract or guarantee future orders. SECTION B � CONTRACT LINE-ITEM NUMBERS (CLINS) CLINs will be established at the order level for administrative categorization. SECTION C � EXECUTION BUSINESS RULES 1. GENERAL RULES The ordering period shall not exceed five (5) years from initial execution (DFARS 216.703(c)). Each BOA will be formally reviewed by the PCO annually (FAR 16.703(c)(2)) and revised as necessary. BOAs shall be changed only by modifying the agreement itself, not by individual orders. Modifications do not apply retroactively to active orders. Prior to the annual review, the PCO will confirm in writing if the contractor wishes to maintain the agreement. Either party may elect not to renew. The Government may cancel the BOA at any time if in its best interest. Only the Army Contracting Command�Rock Island Arsenal (ACC-RIA) is authorized to execute, modify, or perform annual reviews of these master BOAs. Other DoD activities may place orders under these BOAs with ACC-RIA approval. 2. STEP TWO EXECUTED BOAS (QUALIFICATION PHASE) Offerors must demonstrate technical capability by filling out Attachment 001- Purchase Description by answering �Yes� to the items that can be completed and �No� to the items that cannot be completed by offeror. The purchase description at the order level will include but is not limited to the list found in Attachment 001- Purchase Description. 3. STEP THREE ORDER REQUESTS (ORDERING PHASE) Order competitions are limited to active master BOA holders. Order performance periods will be established in each order and remain valid through completion, even if they extend beyond the master BOA's 5-year term. Specific evaluation criteria (e.g., Price-Only, LPTA, or Tradeoff) will be identified in each order�s RFQ. Detail purchase descriptions requirements will be provided at the order level. All orders will be Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP). Work shall not begin until the order is awarded. Business size standards and Non-Manufacturer Rule compliance will be certified and monitored at the order level. Offerors are required to provide pricing catalogs at the order level. SECTION H � SPECIAL CONTRACT REQUIREMENTS 1. CYBERSECURITY MATURITY MODEL CERTIFICATION (CMMC) Conditional Self-Assessment: To be eligible for award, and to remain eligible for orders, the contractor must maintain at least a conditional CMMC Level 2 Self-Assessment in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) at award. Maintenance: Failure to maintain this status will result in immediate restriction from participating in order RFQs, inability to exercise options, and potential removal from the raw metal stock and components BOA. Flow-Down: Subcontractor CMMC requirements (ranging from non-applicable to Level 2) will be defined in individual order solicitations. Primes are solely responsible for subcontractor compliance. 4. SUBCONTRACTING LIMITS AND THE NON-MANUFACTURER RULE (NMR) Limitations on Subcontracting (FAR 52.219-14): Primes must perform at least 50% of the cost of manufacturing (excluding materials) for supply orders. Non-Manufacturer Rule (FAR 52.219-33): Non-manufacturers must supply the product of a domestic small business manufacturer, unless an SBA class or individual waiver applies. title: Design-Build of a Tier II Mobile Command Post Vehicle (MCPV) Trailer
description: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) intends to award a single-award, Firm-Fixed-Price, Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract for Tier II Mobile Command Post Vehicle (MCPV) systems. The purpose of this acquisition is to establish a contract vehicle for the design, engineering, manufacturing, integration, testing, and production of trailer-based mobile command post systems capable of supporting FBI command, control, communications, and computer (C4) operations. The Tier II MCPV requirement consists of a custom-integrated gooseneck trailer system and, when ordered, a compatible Class 4 prime hauler vehicle. The MCPV Trailer shall provide a mobile operational environment supporting mission communications, networking, workspace, power generation and distribution, environmental control, equipment racks, audio/visual capabilities, RF and satellite connectivity provisions, security systems, and integration of Government-furnished and Contractor-furnished mission equipment. The contract will include a First Article requirement. The Contractor shall design, manufacture, integrate, test, and obtain Government approval of an initial MCPV Trailer configuration prior to production quantities. The approved First Article configuration will establish the production baseline for subsequent MCPV Trailer systems. The Government anticipates ordering approximately thirteen (13) MCPV trailer systems and associated prime hauler vehicles over the contract ordering period; however, the Government guarantees only the minimum contract obligation identified in the solicitation. The maximum contract value shall not exceed $15,000,000.00.

title: USCGC HATCHER DryDock Repairs FY27
description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE / REQUEST FOR INFORMATION; not a pre-solicitation notice or solicitation for proposals/quotations. Pursuant to FAR Part 10 (Market Research), the purpose of this notice is to: (1) determine if sources capable of satisfying the agency's requirements exists, (2) determine if commercial items suitable to meet the agency's needs are available or could be modified to meet the agency's requirements, and (3) determine the commercial practices of company's engaged in providing the needed service or supply. Pursuant to FAR Part 6 and FAR Part 19, competition and set-aside decisions may be based on the results of this market research. This notice in no way obligates the Government to any further action. The US Coast Guard, Surface Forces Logistic Center, Alameda CA is seeking contractors interested in providing Maintenance and Repair Services with USCGC HATCHET (WLIC 75309) with USCG 68B BARGE (68019) FY27 DRYDOCK AVAILABILITY. The US Coast Guard Cutter HATCHET (WLIC 75309) is a 75' Inland construction tender class homeported in Galveston, TX. Work list will include but is not limited: inspection, maintenance and preservation of deck equipment, cranes, winches, boat davit, anchor windlass. Cleaning and preservation of various tanks. Deck, structure, and underwater body preservation. There are approximately 88 Line Items. ***PLEASE SEE ATTACHMENT*** 1. A WLIC's design limits its use to protected and inland waters. The cutter is not crewed for continuous steaming and is normally limited to daylight transits. Due to crewing and cutter employment standards, seven days transit is the limit of crew endurance under normal operating conditions. Ten hours of transit per day is the planning factor due to crew fatigue. WLIC's have a maximum speed of 10 knots, however, environmental factors frequently limit average speed to 6.5 knots. 2. Foreseeable costs (crew lodging, messing, rental vehicles, fuel, and authorized crew travel in accordance with the Joint Travel Regulations) will be added to the pricing and will be an economic consideration for award. CUTTER�S HOMEPORT: Galveston, TX. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: Contractor�s Facilities. DESCRIPTION OF WORK: See attached (Rev-0, 24 July 2026) USCGC HATCHET (WLIC 75309) USCG 68B BARGE (68019) SPECIFICATION FOR DRYDOCK REPAIRS FY2027 ***PLEASE SEE ATTACHMENT FOR FULL DETAILS*** ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: 03/09/2027 � 05/19/2027 (70 Days) The applicable NAICS Code is 336611, Ship Building and Repairing, and the size standard is 1,300 employees. SUBMISSION OF INFORMATION: Companies having capabilities necessary to meet or exceed the stated requirements are invited to provide information and a positive statement OF INTEREST, to contribute to this market survey/sources sought notice including commercial market information and company information. Companies may respond to this Sources Sought Notice via e-mail to POC listed in the Contract Opportunities announcement with the following information/documentation: 1. Name of Company, Address and DUNS Number. 2. Point of Contact and Phone Number. 3. Business Size applicable to the NAICS Code: 8(a) Small Business Concern; b. HUBZone Small Business Concern; c. Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business Concern (SDVOSBC); d. Veteran Owned Small Business Concern (VOSBC); e. ED Woman Owned Small Business Concern (EDWOSB); f. Woman Owned Small Business Concern (WOSBC); g. Small Business Concern; h. Large Business Concern. 4. Documentation Verifying Small Business Certification: Please provide the following documentation as it applies to you company. � If claiming 8(a) status, provide a copy of your 8(a) Certificate from SBA. � If claiming HUBZone status, provide a copy of your HUBZone Certificate from SBA. � If claiming SDVOSB status, provide documentation that shows the Service Disable Veteran (SDV) unconditionally owns 51 % of the business, controls the management and daily operations, and holds the highest officer position in the company. Documentation should also be provided to show that the SDV has a service-connected disability that has been determined by the Department of Defense or Department of Veteran Affairs. Finally, provide documentation that shows the business is small under the NAICS code 336611. � If claiming VOSB status, provide documentation that shows the Veteran unconditionally owns 51% of the business, controls the management and daily operation, make long-term decisions for the business, and holds the highest officer position in the company that works at the business fulltime during normal working hours. The documentation should also show the business is small under the NAICS code 336611. � If claiming EDWOSB status, provide documentation that shows the company is at least 51% owned by one or more women who are "economically disadvantaged", and primarily managed by an economically disadvantaged woman that make long-term decisions for the business, hold the highest officer position in the business and work at the business full-time during normal working hours. The documentation should also show the business is small under the NAICS code 336611. A woman is presumed economically disadvantaged if she has a personal net worth of less than $750,000.00 (with some exclusions), her adjusted gross yearly income averaged over the three years preceding the certification less than $350,000.00, and the fair market value of all her assets is less than $6 million. � If claiming Woman Owned Small Business (WOSB) status, provide documentation that shows the company is at least 51% owned and controlled by one or more women, and primarily managed by one or more women that make long-term decisions for the business and hold the highest officer position in the business and work at the business full time during normal working hours. The women must be U.S. citizens. The documentation should also show the business is small under the NAICS code 336611. � If claiming Small Business status, provide documentation to show the business is small under NAICS code 336611. 1. title: Tar Lake Superfund
description: *****Amendment 0002 ***** Amendment 0002 is being issued to respond to additional bidder inquiries, remove Davis-Bacon Construction Wage Determinations MI20260157 and MI20260158 and replace them with Davis-Bacon Construction Wage Determination MI20260043. All other terms and conditions remain UNCHANGED. ***********************Amendment 0001 ******Amendment 0001 is being issued to update the Specifications, Bid Schedule, and Scoping Statement in response to bidder inquiries received. CLIN 0007 is changed from Environmental Remediation Services to Construction. Amendment 0001 also updates the Wage Determinations found in Section L Instructions, Conditions, and Notices to Offerors or Quoters. All other terms and conditions remain UNCHANGED. ********************************************The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Detroit District is seeking a contractor for a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) environmental services contract for the Tar Lake Superfund project located in Mancelona Township, Michigan. The project includes the excavation of contaminated soil and expansion of a bio-sparge system at the Tar Lake Superfund Site in Mancelona Township, Ml. The project will involve excavation of approximately 172,500 tons of contaminated soil, backfilling with clean imported soils, installing new biosparge wells, and an approximately 160 square foot pre-engineered structure to house the biosparge system compressors. Ancillary activities include abandoning existing groundwater monitoring wells, installing new groundwater monitoring wells, installing erosion control measures, conducting a utility survey to locate existing bio-sparge system piping, confirmation soil sampling,and site restoration.

title: 88--Request for Information - Cattle Housing
description: THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS. THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION The Bureau of Land Management is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to identify dairy farms and ranches with the capability and interest to provide temporary housing and care for cattle displaced by recent wildland fires. This RFI is for planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation or commitment for procurement. BACKGROUND Recent wildland fires have significantly impacted ranchers, creating an urgent need for alternative, short and long term cattle housing. The Government is seeking information on facilities that can provide safe, compliant, and reliable support for affected livestock for an estimated period of up to two years. REQUESTED INFORMATION Respondents are asked to provide detailed information regarding their capabilities, including: * Holding capacity (number and type of livestock that can be supported) * Timeframe and length of availability * Animal type preferences (steers, heifers, cows, bred cattle, bulls) * Location and description of facilities * Import requirements and required health certifications * Feed availability * Ability to provide feed onsite or support purchase/transportation * Capacity to store feed on site * Animal health requirements and standards maintained * Ability to separate or isolate cattle from existing herds as required * Veterinary support availability * Identification as a dairy farm or ranch operation ADDITIONAL INFORMATION This RFI is solely intended to gather information. No solicitation is anticipated to be issued, and no contract is anticipated to be awarded as a direct result of this notice. Information received may be shared with impacted ranchers and others, who may independently contact respondents if a need arises. The Capability statements shall be sent by email to judith_chamberlin@ios.doi.gov The capability statement must be submitted by Monday, September 21, 2026 at 1700ES

title: Design-Build of a Tier II Mobile Command Post Trailer
description: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) intends to award a single-award, Firm-Fixed-Price, Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract for Tier II Mobile Command Post Vehicle (MCPV) systems. The purpose of this acquisition is to establish a contract vehicle for the design, engineering, manufacturing, integration, testing, and production of trailer-based mobile command post systems capable of supporting FBI command, control, communications, and computer (C4) operations. The Tier II MCPV requirement consists of a custom-integrated gooseneck trailer system and, when ordered, a compatible Class 4 prime hauler vehicle. The MCPV Trailer shall provide a mobile operational environment supporting mission communications, networking, workspace, power generation and distribution, environmental control, equipment racks, audio/visual capabilities, RF and satellite connectivity provisions, security systems, and integration of Government-furnished and Contractor-furnished mission equipment. The contract will include a First Article requirement. The Contractor shall design, manufacture, integrate, test, and obtain Government approval of an initial MCPV Trailer configuration prior to production quantities. The approved First Article configuration will establish the production baseline for subsequent MCPV Trailer systems. The Government anticipates ordering approximately thirteen (13) MCPV trailer systems and associated prime hauler vehicles over the contract ordering period; however, the Government guarantees only the minimum contract obligation identified in the solicitation. The maximum contract value shall not exceed $15,000,000.00.

title: High Voltage Power Supplies (HVPS) for the Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal (CSSC) Electric Dispersal Barrier
description: The Government has issued an Invitation for Bid (IFB) for the fabrication, pre-acceptance storage, and delivery of six (6) High Voltage Power Supply units for the Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal (CSSC) Electric Dispersal Barrier located in Romeoville, Illinois. PROJECT INFORMATION: This is a solicitation notice for a Non-Commercial Supply contract. The project involves the fabrication of four (4) 1.5 MW and two (2) 350 kW High Voltage Power Supplies, a mandatory twelve (12) month pre-acceptance secure storage period at the contractors facility, an option for six (6) additional months of storage, and final F.o.b. Destination delivery to the operational site. SCOPE OF WORK: The contractor shall furnish all labor, materials, and equipment necessary to manufacture, test, store, and deliver six (6) complete, fully functional HVPS units in strict accordance Scope of Work (SOW). These units are a critical component of the nations aquatic invasive species defense system. This will be a Firm Fixed Price (FFP), IFB procurement in accordance with FAR Part 14, Sealed Bidding. The Government intends to award to the lowest priced bidder deemed responsive and responsible. ACQUISITION INFORMATION: This procurement will be issued on an Unrestricted basis (Full and Open Competition). The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 335314 (Relay and Industrial Control Manufacturing), with a corresponding small business size standard of 750 employees; this is not set-aside to small businesses. One or more of the items under this acquisition is subject to the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement and Free Trade Agreements. No qualification requirement is required in order to be eligible for award; and if so, identify the office from which the qualification requirement may be obtained. All responsible sources may submit a quotation, bid, or proposal, as appropriate, which will be considered by the agency. The award is planned for fourth (4th) quarter of Fiscal Year (FY) 26.IMPORTANT POLICY: Bidders are REQUIRED to be registered and active in the System for Award Management (SAM) at www.sam.gov AT THE TIME a bid is submitted. title: Tar Lake Superfund
description: *****Amendment 0001 ******Amendment 0001 is being issued to update the Specifications, Bid Schedule, and Scoping Statement in response to bidder inquiries received. CLIN 0007 is changed from Environmental Remediation Services to Construction. Amendment 0001 also updates the Wage Determinations found in Section L Instructions, Conditions, and Notices to Offerors or Quoters. All other terms and conditions remain UNCHANGED. ********************************************The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Detroit District is seeking a contractor for a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) environmental services contract for the Tar Lake Superfund project located in Mancelona Township, Michigan. The project includes the excavation of contaminated soil and expansion of a bio-sparge system at the Tar Lake Superfund Site in Mancelona Township, Ml. The project will involve excavation of approximately 172,500 tons of contaminated soil, backfilling with clean imported soils, installing new biosparge wells, and an approximately 160 square foot pre-engineered structure to house the biosparge system compressors. Ancillary activities include abandoning existing groundwater monitoring wells, installing new groundwater monitoring wells, installing erosion control measures, conducting a utility survey to locate existing bio-sparge system piping, confirmation soil sampling,and site restoration.

title: Radar installation kits, management, warehousing/inventory management, and delivery of parts/materials used to overhaul multiple radar antenna systems and fire control systems.
description: Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC) Crane has a requirement to obtain individual hardware items, inspect and determine if the hardware meets the Government requirements, assemble the individual parts into system repair kits, ensure parts within the kits are packed in a manner which prevents damage to the individual parts, that marking practices result in easy identification of the kits and individual parts, the ability to pass on stringent quality requirements to suppliers, warehouse, and deliver parts/materials used to overhaul multiple radar systems and fire control systems. Purpose & Project Scope The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Fort Worth District, in support of Dona Base Camp, NM via Fort Bliss, TX is seeking capabilities statements from qualified firms (both traditional and non-traditional defense contractors) to design and construct a comprehensive set of facilities to support an additional 2,200 soldiers, expanding the camp's capacity to 4,000 to support a full Brigade Combat Team (BCT) during mobilization and rotational training exercises. title: High Voltage Power Supplies (HVPS) for the Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal (CSSC) Electric Dispersal Barrier
description: The Government has issued an Invitation for Bid (IFB) for the fabrication, pre-acceptance storage, and delivery of six (6) High Voltage Power Supply units for the Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal (CSSC) Electric Dispersal Barrier located in Romeoville, Illinois. PROJECT INFORMATION: This is a solicitation notice for a Non-Commercial Supply contract. The project involves the fabrication of four (4) 1.5 MW and two (2) 350 kW High Voltage Power Supplies, a mandatory twelve (12) month pre-acceptance secure storage period at the contractors facility, an option for six (6) additional months of storage, and final F.o.b. Destination delivery to the operational site. SCOPE OF WORK: The contractor shall furnish all labor, materials, and equipment necessary to manufacture, test, store, and deliver six (6) complete, fully functional HVPS units in strict accordance Scope of Work (SOW). description: Design, Development, Engineering, Technical, Programmatic, and Configuration Support Services Task Order in support of Naval Surface Warfare Center, Crane Division, Rapid Mission Integration and Interoperability Department (MX), Model Based Engineering Assessment Division (MXM). title: Non- Standard Weapons (NSW)/ Commercially available M134D Miniguns, Mounts, Support Equipment, Spare Part Kits and Installation/Training Services
description: The purpose of this effort is to issue a sole source solicitation under Title 10 United Stated Code (U.S.C.) �3204(a)(1), as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.103-1(c)(2)(i), substantial duplication of cost to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition to Dillon Aero, Inc. This sole source requirement will result in a Firm Fixed Priced Indefinite Delivery Indefinite contract. The requirement for M134D Minigun weapon systems, along with associated mounting systems for various air/water/ground platforms, parts, accessories, support equipment, installation, and training for operators and maintainers. The M134D variants, including the M134D-H and M134D-M, are 7.62x51mm rotary machine guns. The Government has a need for M134D variants as they are capable of delivering precision and rapid fire on personnel and vehicle-sized (2m x 3m) materiel targets with fixed firing rates of 3,000 rounds per minute. The M134D-H is a hybrid design that utilizes titanium and skeletonized parts to offer increased weight savings of 10-20 pounds while retaining the longer service life of the steel gun. The M134D-M (marinized) variation utilizes ceramic coatings to improve corrosion resistance for use in the marine environment. Spare parts and accessories are also required for each configuration and will be incorporated into the contract. Installation and training services will be included for platform installation (air/ground/water platforms) and operator and maintainer training courses.

description: This is a contract for mess attendant support services for the Berg-Liles Dining Facility which will remain under the full operational and management control of the 325th Fighter Wing Force Support Squadron (FSS), Tyndall AFB, FL. Management and operational control retained by the 325th FSS will include but is not limited to all management responsibility, oversight and decision-making authority of the day-to-day operations of the dining facility including establishing operational hours, budgeting, accounting and recordkeeping, storeroom management, and other management functions. At no time shall the contractor exercise any operational control of the dining facility in the performance of this contract. The contractor shall perform the requirements in the PWS IAW Tri-Service Food Code and conform to the professional standards identified in this contract. Furthermore, the contractor shall follow all applicable federal laws, regulations, instructions and directives as identified in the PWS. Contractor tasks include, but not limited to, the following: serving and replenishing food; cleaning interior and exterior of facilities, equipment, and utensils; maintain equipment and repair as required; preparing raw vegetables and fruits for the self-serve bars and for use by military cooks; preparing cold cuts and cheeses for the use by military cooks at the sandwich/deli bar; ensure coverage for ethnic and/or specialty food bars; make and wrap sandwiches; cut and portion pastry items and provide cashier services. description: The Mobile District COE has a need for one MATOC for a full range of horizontal construction, renovation, repair, and some incidental design task orders for general construction primarily at 12 locations in AL, FL, GA, and MS. title: Crash Attenuating Seat Assemblies Structural Fabrication and Installation Airbus AS-332L1 Super Puma Helicopter
description: USDA Forest Service Procurement & Property Services, Incident Procurement Operations, Aviation Branch intends to procure, by means of other than full and open competition Airbus AS-332L1 Super Puma Helicopter. The intent is to negotiate a two-phase firm fixed price purchase order with Precision Integrated Programs, LLC., to procure Crash Attenuating Seat Assemblies Structural Fabrication and Installation on an Airbus AS-332L1 Super Puma Helicopter. This service includes the following: Phase I - Manufacturing: The offeror shall manufacture all parts/placards/assemblies required for one full installation of crash attenuating seats. Phase II - Assembly and Installation: The offeror shall hold an FAA part 145 Certified Repair Station (CRS) certificate with an Airframe Class 4 rating or Super Puma helicopter limited rating. The firm fixed purchase order will be for the services provided herein. The anticipated award date is October 1, 2026. This is a sole source solicitation to Precision Integrated Programs, LLC. No other sources will be considered. This requirement is not set aside for small business.
